claims.value: Member of the Latin Monetary Union, whose participating states coordinated gold and silver coin standards.

scope.description: Named historical state or institutional/person association; no statistical or polygon-wide inference.

evidence.note: NBB explicitly identifies Belgium, Switzerland, France, Italy and Greece as participants. Conservative interior excludes founding and dissolution years; neither banknote union nor political federation is asserted.

qualifications: Year precision retained. Bounded research interval is not an assertion that the historical institution or person began or ended at its research cutoff.

origin.reference: Regional Batch 01 original institutional source review

claims.value: Linked to the other state through the Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU).

scope.description: Named historical state or institutional/person association; no statistical or polygon-wide inference.

evidence.locator: The treaty of the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union – 1921
evidence.note: Official history identifies the treaty and continuing economic and monetary ties. The conservative 1923 start avoids treating signature in 1921 as commencement in that year; no sovereign merger is implied.

qualifications: Year precision retained. Bounded research interval is not an assertion that the historical institution or person began or ended at its research cutoff.

claims.value: Party to the signed 1944 Benelux Customs Agreement with the other two Benelux states; the customs union was not yet implemented during this interval.

scope.description: Named historical state or institutional/person association; no statistical or polygon-wide inference.

evidence.note: Signed agreement is distinguished from customs union implementation. No functioning customs union is projected into 1945.

qualifications: Year precision retained. Bounded research interval is not an assertion that the historical institution or person began or ended at its research cutoff.
